data.why: The repo bundles a sample daily precipitation Excel file (Year/Month/Day/Precipitation columns) loadable both via the in-app 'load sample' button and as an upload, so no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Load an annual maximum precipitation/discharge series and preview it before analysis
Group and aggregate a raw daily series into an annual maximum series for flood-frequency analysis
Fit theoretical distributions (Gumbel, Pearson III, GEV, Krytsky-Menkel) to the series and compare them against the empirical exceedance points
Inspect goodness-of-fit metrics (R2, MAE, maxE, Anderson-Darling) to choose the best-fitting distribution
Read off a design value for a given exceedance probability or return period (e.g. the 1% / 100-year flow)
Export the fitted curves, parameter tables and quantile tables as a Word report

review.summary: The goal and four phases match the README's upload → prepare → process → results workflow and the job of flood/precipitation frequency analysis, and the screens I sampled match their nodes. The tool's central output, the exceedance plot with fitted curves and a return-period axis, is missing as both task and feature because it never rendered, so the tree needs that addition plus a few structural fixes before filing.
